column1: IP Phone Instrument Validation Update & Duplicate Product Addition Remediation
column36:
The product “inContact IP VOICE + SETUP (12630)” is being repeatedly re-added to accounts in Cadebill for the Intuitive Surgical BU after it has been end-dated. Because the additions are not immediately visible in day-to-day workflows, the condition may have persisted for some time and has created confusion and potential duplicate product records on the account.
Investigation established that the product is being added manually through a provisioning request submitted in the Cadebill UI, which is then processed by the SDP service. A specific manual request was traced to Javier in Order Management. The Cadebill, SCP, and adjacent engineering teams each confirmed that no recent code or configuration changes were made to this product, which points to process and validation logic rather than a regression as the root cause.
The Provisioning team does not have permission to add products directly. When provisioning a new instrument, Provisioning must ask Order Management to add any required products. If a validation check fails during instrument addition, this handoff results in a manual product addition — which is the mechanism by which the end-dated product is reintroduced.
The controlling validation logic for adding an instrument of type “inContact IP phone” (instrument type 12709) currently checks for the presence of SKUs 1283447 and 1283448. Both SKUs are now obsolete, so the check no longer reflects the current product catalog and drives incorrect provisioning outcomes. The agreed direction is to replace these checks with the current product and feature keys: SKUs 12646 and 1285 and their child SKUs (for example 12841281 and 12841282). The exact OR/AND condition structure will be confirmed against the current implementation.

column1: (Phase 1) Credit Memo Automation Workato Recipes
column36:
Recipe A — Cadebill to Salesforce
Trigger: MCL Cadebill API call when billing team submits a credit request (either path).
Action: Updates the Invoice Adjustment case in Salesforce with credit payload. Triggers the Salesforce approval queue routing.
Applies to: Both line-item credits (Invoice Adjustment screen) and account-level credits (Payments/Adjustments screen). The 'Submission Path' field in the payload distinguishes the two.

Recipe B — Salesforce to Cadebill
Trigger: Salesforce approval completion event on the Invoice Adjustment case.
Action: Pushes the approval result (approved/rejected, approver details, timestamp) back to Cadebill via MCL's sync-back API. Cadebill then triggers the publication queue for approved memos, or returns rejected submissions to Draft status.

Key Design Constraints
•	Both recipes are one-directional per transfer — no polling loops within a single recipe run
•	Both recipes must be idempotent — retrying must not create duplicate approvals 
•	No business logic in Workato — all rules enforced by source/destination systems
•	Error states must be logged and alerted — no silent failures
•	Recipes are maintained by MIS post go-live

column1: Minimum‑Related Case Intake and Routing
column36:
Sales representatives currently submit minimum‑related inquiries through existing Sales Operations case channels, which results in mixed routing, delayed response times, and lack of ownership clarity. Finance leadership has requested a more structured approach to ensure that minimum‑specific inquiries are handled separately and efficiently.

This project will introduce either:

A separate case submission path for minimum‑related inquiries, or
Enhanced routing logic within existing Sales Ops cases to automatically identify and route minimum‑related cases.
Additionally, Orr has requested the creation of a dedicated case queue for minimum inquiries, which sales representatives can use when opening cases. These cases will route directly to James Boase for handling.

Due to the need for Salesforce configuration and/or development, this work must be initiated as a formal MIS project and aligned with Finance priorities, as confirmed by Robert.
column97: Business GoalProvide a clear, efficient, and Finance-aligned way for Sales Representatives to submit minimum-related inquiries in Salesforce and ensure those cases are routed correctly without manual intervention.Customer Need:A clear submission path for minimum-related casesCorrect and consistent routing aligned to Finance ownershipReduced delays and rework caused by manual reassignmentVisibility and reporting on minimum-related inquiriesElimination of manual triage burden on Sales Operations and TAM teamsThis request was raised by Orr and is confirmed as part of Finance priorities by Robert.Solution DetailsThe proposed solution is to enhance the existing Salesforce case intake flow to support minimum-specific case handling. Based on the May 28 discovery discussion, the preferred approach is to piggyback on the existing Sales Operations case process rather than create a new case type or separate submission path. This avoids architectural complexity while achieving the desired routing outcome.At a high level, the solution will:Provide Sales Representatives with a clear method to submit cases related to minimums within the existing Sales Ops case submission flowIntroduce a new initial categorization option (e.g., “Contracted Minimum Inquiry”) within the existing case submission flowAutomatically route minimum-related cases to a dedicated Minimum Inquiries queue, owned by James BoaseKeep the case record type as Sales Ops (consistent with the existing model, similar to CPQ Admin queue escalations)Implementation ApproachThe existing Sales Ops case submission experience is a guided flow (not direct Case object creation). Sales reps access it via a button on the relevant Salesforce record (Opportunity, Account, or Quote). The flow presents context-specific initial categorization options based on the record type selected.Technical DetailsHigh-level technical considerations include:Salesforce Case ConfigurationCase Record Type:No new case record type required. Cases will remain Sales Ops record type, consistent with the existing model.New initial categorization option added to the Sales Ops case submission flow under the 'Account' optionOption label to be confirmed “Contracted Minimum Inquiry” under the 'Initial Categorization' drop-down﻿Routing & AssignmentCreate a new dedicated Minimum Inquiries queue in SalesforceQueue ownership assigned to James BoaseAutomated assignment rule or flow logic to route cases with the new categorization to this queueManual fallback: if a case is misdirected, Sales Ops teams (Angie’s and Hugo’s) and James Boase can manually reassign, consistent with current practiceAutomationDeclarative automation preferred (e.g., Record-Triggered Flow or Assignment Rule)Logic to detect the “Contracted Minimum Inquiry” initial categorization and route to the Minimum Inquiries queueNo manual queue management required by Sales Ops teams for correctly submitted casesReporting & VisibilityCases in the Minimum Inquiries queue will be filterable and reportable independently from standard Sales Ops casesThe Minimum Inquiries queue is expected to be excluded from Sales Ops SLA reporting in the same manner as CPQ Admin queue escalations are currently excludedFinance oversight and prioritization of minimum inquiries supported through queue-based reportingGovernanceConfiguration-first approach; custom development only if required following architectural reviewMust adhere to MIS development and deployment standardsAngie Draper and Hugo Pineda (Sales Ops team leads) to review and sign off on the design before implementation proceedsStakeholdersRequestor: OrrFinance Priority Owner: Jason W.Queue Owner: James BoaseImpacted Teams:FinanceSales OperationsMIS / Salesforce Administration

# *Attachments should not be archived for open cases.*
Cases that remain open for more than two months are typically complex and involve ongoing exchanges of information, logs, and documents between the customer and the support engineer. Archiving attachments for actively open cases disrupts the investigation process and reduces efficiency.

If archiving is required, it would be more appropriate to apply it only to cases in statuses(in addition to *closed)* such as *Pending Software Release* or *Resolved.*

# *Retrieved attachments should retain and display their original upload date.*
When attachments are restored, the system should reflect the actual date and time the file was originally uploaded to Wiser, regardless of whether it was uploaded by the customer or by a support engineer. Preserving the original timestamp would allow engineers to easily understand the sequence of events and maintain the correct chronology of attachments when working on long-running cases.

h3. *1. Change Title*

Refinement of *“iT Support”* Deployment Group (# IT-Support-AI-PROD) Logic using Common Organizational Group

Standard Change (Low Risk – Controlled logic update)

h3. *3. Description of Change*

The current IT Support Deployment group membership is derived from multiple dependent groups created for periodic production deployments and dynamic attributes such as ELT hierarchy and manager chain mapping.

The proposed change will replace the existing logic with a simplified structure by leveraging a *single centralized group: _ “# NiCE All Staff”*, which contains all active employees.

This change aims to standardize access provisioning by removing dependency on multiple groups and dynamic attributes.

h3. *4. Current State (As-Is)*

* Group membership derived from:
** Multiple deployment-specific groups
** Attribute-based conditions (ELT, manager hierarchy)
* Frequent changes in attributes lead to:
** Inconsistent group membership
** Risk of permission loss during organizational/Attribute changes

h3. *5. Proposed State (To-Be)*

* Replace current logic with:
** Single group: *“NiCE All Staff”*
* All employees (including new joiners) will inherit access via this centralized group
* Eliminate dependency on:
** ELT/manager attributes
** Temporary deployment groups

h3. *6. Business Justification / Reason for Change*

* Prevent access/permission loss caused by attribute changes
* Improve stability of IT Support deployment access
* Ensure seamless onboarding experience (automatic inclusion of new joiners)
* Reduce operational complexity and dependency on multiple groups
* Align with *centralized access management best practices*

column1: MW - change in the logic for Impacted CI's
column36:
h2. *Summary*

Enhance Maintenance Window logic to align case suppression and instance sub-status with Change Request lifecycle

----

h2. *Description*

The current Maintenance Window logic sets the instance sub-status (In maintenance) based on the start and end of the maintenance window itself. This approach creates inaccuracies when multiple maintenance windows overlap on the same instance or when multiple change requests occur at different times within a maintenance.

To address this, the logic should be updated so that instance sub-status and case suppression are driven by the lifecycle of associated Change Requests rather than the maintenance window duration.

----

h2. *Context*

During analysis, it was identified that:

* An instance can be part of multiple maintenance windows simultaneously. When one maintenance ends while another is still active, the system removes the sub-status incorrectly and resumes case creation.
* Alerts triggered during ongoing work can therefore generate unwanted cases, even though maintenance activity is still in progress. 

Additionally:

* A single maintenance window may include multiple change requests with different execution times. 
* Current behavior does not reflect the actual work timeline at the change level, leading to inaccurate monitoring suppression. 

----

h2. *Solution*

Update system behavior to align instance sub-status and case suppression with Change Request lifecycle:

# *Trigger Sub-status Based on Change Lifecycle*
#* When a Change Request moves to *“Implement”*, apply sub-status (Downtime CR) to relevant instances. 
#* When the Change Request moves to *“Review”*, remove the sub-status. 
# *Decouple from Maintenance Start/End*
#* Remove existing logic that applies/removes sub-status based on maintenance window timing. 
# *Maintenance Completion Validation*
#* When attempting to end a maintenance:
#** If any associated Change Request is still in “Implement”:
#*** Display a warning notification to the user “Please note, CR # (can be multiples) is still in Implement state”
# *Notification / Governance Enhancements (Optional)*
#* Ensure visibility if:
#** Change Requests are not moved to “Implement” after maintenance start.
#** Maintenance is being closed while active changes still exist. 
# *Scope Enforcement*
#* Validation applies *only to Change Requests linked to the maintenance window*, not unrelated changes. 



IMPORTANT! Please note: when we built the CR substatus with Tzeela (CR 19130) we exclude CR related to MW, we just need to remove this exclusion and it will work.

----

h2. *Acceptance Criteria*

h3. *AC1 – Sub-status driven by Change Request*

* GIVEN a Change Request linked to a maintenance
* WHEN the Change moves to *Implement*
* THEN the instance sub-status is set to Downtime CR (like any other CR)
* GIVEN the Change moves to *Review*
* THEN the instance sub-status is removed

----

h3. *AC2 – Removal of Maintenance-based Logic*

* GIVEN a maintenance window starts or ends
* THEN no sub-status changes occur unless triggered by a Change Request

----

h3. *AC3 – Case Suppression Accuracy*

* GIVEN an instance has at least one Change in “Implement”
* THEN alerts do NOT generate cases
* GIVEN no active Change in “Implement”
* THEN alerts generate cases normally

----

h3. *AC4 – Maintenance Closure Validation*

* GIVEN a user attempts to end a maintenance
* AND at least one Change is still in “Implement”
* THEN the system:
** Shows a warning requiring user acknowledgment

----

h3. *AC5 – No Impact from Overlapping Maintenance*

* GIVEN multiple maintenance windows exist on the same instance
* THEN sub-status behavior is controlled only by Change Requests

----

h3. *AC6 – Scope Control*

* GIVEN Change Requests not linked to the maintenance
* THEN they are NOT considered in validation or sub-status logic

----

h3. *AC67 – System warning* 

* when a MW is move to Start and End there is a warning to say that Instances will be in sub-status, need to remove that, and add a sentence to MWM to ensure that users will change CR to implement.

----

h2. *Additional Details / Considerations*

* *Operational benefit:*
** Eliminates false case creation during ongoing maintenance work
** Improves monitoring accuracy and alert suppression
* *Process alignment:*
** Fully aligns with standard Change Management lifecycle (Implement → Review).
* *Edge cases to consider:*
** Very large maintenance scopes (e.g., thousands of CIs) may impact performance
** Users must follow correct Change lifecycle updates to avoid unintended alerts
* *Interim workaround (current state):*
** Manage all related work within a single maintenance window to avoid duplicate behavior issues.

Is there any way to make the _Database_ field off of the Instance record read-only and derive it from the Database CI item. They may have been SQL Server at some point and maybe the record never got updated. There is nothing stopping someone from going in there and changing the _database_ field back to SQL Server. So having some data validation there or deriving it form the other field would be a good enhancement.

 

Just thought I’d send it along. It is not a huge issue, but it would be good if this value could be derived from the CI database item.

column1: Playwright Claude Desktop MCP
column36:
[https://playwright.dev/mcp/introduction|https://playwright.dev/mcp/introduction|smart-link] 

Confirmed the technical shape. Before I build: an org-level custom connector in Claude Desktop/Cowork requires a *remote HTTPS MCP server* — you can't point it at a local {{npx}} process. So this means hosting Playwright MCP yourself, with the browser running server-side (headless, in the cloud), not on your laptop.

Three decisions I need from you:Now installing deps and compiling to catch real errors before I write the infra.Final verification pass — rebuilding clean, re-running both auth modes, and checking a real browser action end to end.Built and tested. Two things you should know before deploying:

*The constraint that shaped everything.* Claude's org connectors only accept a remote HTTPS MCP URL. Playwright MCP is a local stdio server, so it can't be added directly — it has to be hosted. This wraps it in an Entra ID OAuth gateway on Azure Container Apps. Consequence: the browser runs in Azure, not on anyone's laptop. It can't reach NiCE intranet systems, and it starts with no logged-in sessions. If your actual goal is automating internal web apps, Claude in Chrome is the better fit — this is right for public-web work.

*Why there's a bridge in there.* Entra doesn't support Dynamic Client Registration or the RFC 8707 {{resource}} parameter that MCP clients send. The gateway fronts Entra to paper over both, which also keeps the client secret inside the container instead of pasted into Claude's settings. {{AUTH_MODE=direct}} is the simpler fallback if that misbehaves.

What I verified locally: TypeScript builds clean, MCP handshake and all 42 tools proxy through correctly, SSE streams, session headers pass through, a real {{tools/call}} round-trips, the 401 challenge carries the right {{WWW-Authenticate}} header, and every OAuth endpoint returns valid documents in both auth modes.

What I could *not* verify: an actual browser launch. This sandbox's network allowlist blocked the Chromium download (403 from {{cdn.playwright.dev}}). The tool call reached Playwright and returned a clean "browser not installed" error, so the plumbing is proven — but the first real end-to-end browser run will happen on your Azure build. Section 7 of the README covers what to check if it doesn't.

Deploy is {{./infra/01-entra-setup.sh}} then {{./infra/02-deploy-aca.sh}}, plus one manual admin-consent click in the portal.

One flag for whoever signs off: you picked the full tool set, which includes {{browser_evaluate}} and {{browser_run_code_unsafe}} — arbitrary JS and arbitrary Playwright code in that container, available to anyone in the org who enables the connector. Section 6 lays out the containment options. Narrowing to a read-only subset later is a small change if you want it.

column1: New API for MW customer exclusion validation
column36:
h2. *Summary*

Create new API to validate that a customer is fully excluded from a Maintenance Window (MW)

----

h2. *Context / Description*

Excluding a customer from a Maintenance Window (MW) is a *critical and sensitive action*, as it requires the customer to be *fully removed from all MW execution scopes*.

Currently, there is *no automated validation mechanism* for Cloud Operations to confirm that a customer who requested exclusion has been *completely removed from the MW impacted customers list*.

This creates risks such as:

* Partial exclusion (customer still present in MW scope)
* Inconsistent execution of maintenance activities
* Lack of validation and audit capability

----

h3. *Objective*

Introduce a new API that enables Cloud Operations to *verify exclusion status* by checking whether a customer + solution combination is still present in the MW impacted customers list.

----

h2. *Acceptance Criteria*

h3. *1. API Creation*

* A new API endpoint is created to validate MW exclusion status

----

h3. *2. API Input Parameters*

The API must accept the following inputs:

* *Dates* (mandatory) 

----

*3. Output:*

* *Customer Name* 
* *Instances ID* 
* *Oracle Customer Number* 
* *Solution* 

----

h3. *4. Validation Logic*

Upon API call:

* System navigates to:
** MW → *“Impacted Customers Solution”* data source
* System checks:
** If *Customer + Solution combination exists* in the MW

----

h3. *5. API Response Logic*

h4. *If Customer is NOT found:*

* Return: *Positive result (Excluded = TRUE)*
* Meaning:
** Customer is fully excluded from MW

h4. *If Customer IS found:*

* Return: *Negative result (Excluded = FALSE)*
* Meaning:
** Customer is still part of MW scope

*NSC Approval → Workato → IDM (v4.0):*

# Existing 'Request for Wiser permission' NSC catalog item and division-based automated approval (KB0011070) used unchanged — no development required for this step.

If count >= baseline: provisioning blocked, NSC ticket updated (exact behaviour per OI-01 resolution). If within limit: proceeds to IDM call.
# Workato calls IDM/NetIQ Manager REST API with employee number and user type. IDM: if account absent, creates it; if present, updates permissions. IDM returns success or failure to Workato.

13/Jan/25 12:56 PM;621f1c4f94f7e20069fdd50c;*Meeting Summary:*

*Meeting Purpose:*
Michael outlined the purpose of the meeting, which is to request a proactive report to identify and resolve rates and charges errors (101 and 102) before the billing cycle begins. Addressing errors in advance aims to smoothen the billing process.

*Report Request:*
Michael emphasized the importance of generating a report that highlights errors before the billing cycle, as the current reports only capture errors after the cycle runs. This proactive measure will allow for timely corrections.

*Error 101 Explanation:*
Swati explained that error code 101 occurs when no recurring charge campaign is available, typically due to manual errors by agents. She suggested generating a report to check if scheduled campaigns or rate plans are mapped to products and sending it to the concerned team for fixing.

* *Cause of Error 101:* Missing scheduled campaigns or rate plans due to manual agent errors.
* *Proposed Solution:* Generate a report to identify such issues before the billing cycle, ensuring they are corrected beforehand.

*Error 102 Explanation:*
Swati further explained that error code 102 arises when a scheduled campaign is defined but lacks a set date. This causes errors for all accounts linked to the product mapped to that campaign.

* *Cause of Error 102:* Scheduled campaigns without a set date.
* *Proposed Solution:* Apply logic to ensure all SKUs are defined inside the scheduled campaign with correct dates, preventing errors.

*Report Scheduling:*
It was discussed the need to schedule the error reports to run before each billing cycle. Swati proposed automating the process by creating a job for this, while Michael suggested running the reports on a weekly basis rather than daily to avoid redundancy.

* *Agreement:* Reports will be scheduled weekly, not daily, to identify and correct errors before the billing cycle.

*Report Creation Timeline:*
Michael inquired about the time required to create these reports. Swati will check with the team and provide an update by the end of the day or tomorrow.

*Documentation Request:*
Dana requested that Swati prepare a small design document outlining the job, its frequency, and execution details for documentation purposes. Swati agreed to provide this before starting the task.

*Weekly Job Agreement:*
Manimaran agreed to the weekly job proposal, suggesting it be scheduled for Fridays or Sundays. They also mentioned the possibility of manually creating the job if required.

*Meeting Conclusion:*

09/Apr/25 2:52 PM;621f1c4f94f7e20069fdd50c;Hi @Henry Miles,

We checked more on this.

Implementing tax configuration at provider-based logic will require more time, and require lots of validation.

 

Instead, we are considering adding a new option for "Canada (Non-Taxable)" country. And put all the Canadian Accounts into that, that are not assigned with a Provider. This will allow accounts that do not require calling the SureTax API to be categorized under this option.

column508:
22/Apr/25 1:53 PM;621f1c4f94f7e20069fdd50c;I have attached a PowerPoint that explains how taxes are done during invoice generation. Please review and also see our answers below.

 

This would be helpful, however it still does not prevent other countries from being sent through. Is there any workaround for other providers outside of Canada?

*As explained before, accounts that are set with taxable country of Countries that are added under "Company Tax Method" with "Tax Method" as SureTax, only would be sent to SureTax API for tax calculations.*

*Currently it is set with countries USA and Canada. So other countries are not set to SureTax.*

 

The issue is two-fold, 1) is the taxes that are being charged on Canadian accounts that shouldn’t be, but 2) is the fact that sending through customers in other countries shows up as revenue going through Suretax, even if ST doesn’t rate or return any taxes on the invoices. It still counts as revenues Suretax see on their end, and that in turn increases the total amount of our annual agreement (and overages) that we have with Suretax – our annual agreement is based on total dollar amount sent through for processing.

*For this reason, we have suggested to add a new country by name "Canada (Non-Taxable)" and put all the non-taxable Canadian Accounts into that, that are assigned with a Provider. And these accounts would not be sent through SureTax API. And rest of the Canadian accounts only will be sent for SureTax processing.*



Any other workarounds or ideas for how to prevent this?

*The approach suggested above is a good solution.*

 

I believe we can manually exempt individual accounts in CB so they don’t go through the API, but this will require a lot of manual work any time a new account is set up, and could also cause issues if accounts switch between providers (from US billing to international or vice versa).

*While setting tax exemption at the account level is an option, it is also possible that the setting may get missed for international accounts. That’s why "Canada (Non-Taxable)" would be the best option. We can also setup a job to automatically set the taxable country to “Canada (Non-Taxable)” for international accounts, as a failover option to catch all those accounts that were not correctly setup with taxable country.*

05/Sep/26 1:48 PM;621f1c4f94f7e20069fdd50c;Checked the record directly (sys_user table, Wiser/niceprod instance). Here's what I found for {{PublicSafetyStratusAppsDevTeam@nice.com}} (sys_id {{5be4876c1b05619c6d15ecea234bcbed}}):

* {{web_service_access_only}} = *true* right now
* {{last_login}} / {{last_login_time}} = *2026-06-05 17:35:54*, with a string of earlier updates through May 2026 (05-06, 05-07, 05-11, 05-14, 05-19, 05-21, 05-22, 06-02, 06-05)
* {{failed_attempts}} also incremented a few times in June (06-10, 06-23) — consistent with attempted logins failing
* The record's most recent update (2026-09-02 19:03) was a change to the {{u_rd_users}} (responsible users) field, not the web-service flag
* Pulling the audit trail specifically for the {{web_service_access_only}} field on this record returned *zero entries* — no recorded change to that flag at any point since the record was created in 2023

So I can't confirm from the audit log that the flag was flipped recently, or a "before/after" moment tied to the login error. It's either been {{true}} since 2023 and unaudited, or something changed it without leaving a field-level audit trail (not every field is audited by default in ServiceNow).

One caveat worth flagging: {{last_login_time}} in ServiceNow isn't a clean signal of "this account logged into the UI interactively." Per ServiceNow's own community discussions, that field also gets updated by things like an admin impersonating the user, or other background/read-access triggers — not just a genuine interactive session by the account itself. So the presence of login timestamps doesn't necessarily contradict the webservice-only flag being in effect; it may reflect impersonation or another indirect trigger rather than the service account itself opening a UI session.

Given that, I'd treat this as inconclusive rather than proof the account had normal interactive access while flagged. To settle it definitively you'd want someone with admin access to check whether {{web_service_access_only}} is set to be audited in the dictionary, or pull actual session/transaction logs (not just the {{last_login*}} fields) for that user around those May/June dates.

h2. Requirements

*Purpose:*

The *NSC Tickets Agent* (Incident or Request) enables BA CS and BA Cadebill teams to resolve NSC tickets faster by retrieving historically similar tickets from ServiceNow and presenting AI‑assisted resolution recommendations.

The agent analyses and classifies the ticket, assigns it to a generic user, automatically updates its status, and based on the ticket description, generates a structured set of recommended insights.

 

*High-Level Behavior:*

* When an Incident or Request is assigned to the BA CS, BA Cadebill, or BA Fin Cadebill teams, the agent automatically classifies the ticket and assigns it to the designated user (Eitan Fireberg).
* The agent updates the ticket status to “Pending Future Activities” and sets a target date two weeks from the creation date.
* The agent changes the ticket status to “Pending Future Activities” with a Target Date of 2 weeks ahead.
* The agent is integrated with all NSC tickets managed by these teams.
* Upon assignment, the agent searches for historically similar NSC tickets and provides references to related cases, along with recommended next steps or resolution actions. These insights are automatically added to the ticket’s Work Notes.

column1: Hash session keys in Redis token store — raw JWTs/refresh tokens stored as plaintext keys
column36:
*Summary:* Hash session keys in Redis token store — raw JWTs/refresh tokens stored as plaintext keys

*Type:* Bug (Security) · *Priority:* High

*Description:*The Redis token store uses the raw Entra JWT as the session key name, and stores MCP refresh tokens (and migration/alias values) as plaintext keys and values. Live credentials are therefore exposed to anyone with Redis data-plane read access, backups, SLOWLOG/MONITOR, or the {{inspect_redis.py}} output — contradicting the "encrypted at rest / plaintext never persisted" claim in the docs. Fernet only encrypts the value blob, not the keys.

*Fix:* Hash all key names (HMAC-SHA256 + pepper), Fernet-encrypt cross-reference values and SET members. Public API stays unchanged. Ship with dual-read migration to avoid mass logout, and update the false docs claims.

*Acceptance criteria:*

* No raw JWT or refresh token appears as a Redis key, value, or SET member ({{SCAN}} test asserts no {{eyJ...}} matches).
* Full JWT-rotation cycle works (old + new bearer resolve during alias window).
* Live sessions survive deploy via dual-read.
* Docs corrected ({{README}} L325, {{redis_token_store.py}} L8–11, {{auth-flow.md}} L121).

column1: New SR for MW exclusion
column36:
h3. *Summary*

Create new SR type: *Request for Maintenance Exclusion* with approval workflow

----

h3. *Description*

h4. *Context*

Excluding a customer from a Maintenance Window (MW) is a *high-risk and sensitive activity*, as it results in the customer being *fully removed from the MW scope* and *not receiving maintenance actions*.

Currently, there is no standardized and governed process to manage such exclusions, creating:

* Risk of unintended service gaps
* Lack of visibility and accountability
* No formal approval or audit trail

----

h4. *Solution*

Introduce a new SR item in the catalogue for *GCO and ACO (all solutions)* with:

* Standardized intake form
* Defined routing logic
* Approval workflow with required justification
* Automated notifications



Open the new SR: *TAM and CSM* (mean that we need to have it in the portal request, the customers *CANNOT* request by themselve)

----

h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

h4. *1. SR Catalog*

* New item in the catalog created:
** *Request for Maintenance Exclusion*
* Available for:
** GCO and ACO
** All solutions
** Access to TAM, CSM (external view) and technical view catalogue 

----

h4. *2. Form Fields*

The SR form includes:

* Requestor (auto-populated)
* Customer (mandatory)
* Solution (mandatory)
* Instance
** Auto-derived based on *Customer + Solution*
* Reason for Exclusion (mandatory, free text)
* MW Exclusion Date (mandatory)

----

h4. *3. Routing Logic*

* ACO solutions → assigned to *Gilbert Laun*
* GCO solutions → assigned to *Rohit Jagtap*

----

h4. *4. Notifications (Submission)*

Triggered upon submission:

* Assigned approver
* MWM
* Requestor

----

h4. *5. Review Process*

* MWM schedules review with manager
* Purpose:
** Ensure requestor understands:
*** Impact of exclusion
*** Risks to MW operations

----

h4. *6. Approval Decision*

*Approved:*

* Customer excluded from MW
* Notification sent:
** Requestor
** MWM

*Declined:*

* Approver must provide rejection reason (mandatory)
* Notification sent:
** Requestor
** Includes decline reason

----

h3. *Other Information / Notes*

* This process enforces *governance over MW exclusions*
* Ensures *no customer is excluded without visibility*
* Reduces operational risk and improves accountability

column1: Fix instance status handling for overlapping Maintenance Windows
column36:
h2. *Summary*

Enhance Maintenance Window logic to align case suppression and instance sub-status with Change Request lifecycle

----

h2. *Description*

The current Maintenance Window logic sets the instance sub-status (In maintenance) based on the start and end of the maintenance window itself. This approach creates inaccuracies when multiple maintenance windows overlap on the same instance or when multiple change requests occur at different times within a maintenance.

To address this, the logic should be updated so that instance sub-status and case suppression are driven by the lifecycle of associated Change Requests rather than the maintenance window duration.

----

h2. *Context*

During analysis, it was identified that:

* An instance can be part of multiple maintenance windows simultaneously. When one maintenance ends while another is still active, the system removes the sub-status incorrectly and resumes case creation.
* Alerts triggered during ongoing work can therefore generate unwanted cases, even though maintenance activity is still in progress. 

Additionally:

* A single maintenance window may include multiple change requests with different execution times. 
* Current behavior does not reflect the actual work timeline at the change level, leading to inaccurate monitoring suppression. 

----

h2. *Solution*

Update system behavior to align instance sub-status and case suppression with Change Request lifecycle:

# *Trigger Sub-status Based on Change Lifecycle*
#* When a Change Request moves to *“Implement”*, apply sub-status (Downtime CR) to relevant instances. 
#* When the Change Request moves to *“Review”*, remove the sub-status. 
# *Decouple from Maintenance Start/End*
#* Remove existing logic that applies/removes sub-status based on maintenance window timing. 
# *Maintenance Completion Validation*
#* When attempting to end a maintenance:
#** If any associated Change Request is still in “Implement”:
#*** Display a warning notification to the user “Please note, CR # (can be multiples) is still in Implement state”
# *Notification / Governance Enhancements (Optional)*
#* Ensure visibility if:
#** Change Requests are not moved to “Implement” after maintenance start.
#** Maintenance is being closed while active changes still exist. 
# *Scope Enforcement*
#* Validation applies *only to Change Requests linked to the maintenance window*, not unrelated changes. 



IMPORTANT! Please note: when we built the CR substatus with Tzeela (CR 19130) we exclude CR related to MW, we just need to remove this exclusion and it will work.

----

h2. *Acceptance Criteria*

h3. *AC1 – Sub-status driven by Change Request*

* GIVEN a Change Request linked to a maintenance
* WHEN the Change moves to *Implement*
* THEN the instance sub-status is set to Downtime CR (like any other CR)
* GIVEN the Change moves to *Review*
* THEN the instance sub-status is removed

----

h3. *AC2 – Removal of Maintenance-based Logic*

* GIVEN a maintenance window starts or ends
* THEN no sub-status changes occur unless triggered by a Change Request

----

h3. *AC3 – Case Suppression Accuracy*

* GIVEN an instance has at least one Change in “Implement”
* THEN alerts do NOT generate cases
* GIVEN no active Change in “Implement”
* THEN alerts generate cases normally

----

h3. *AC4 – Maintenance Closure Validation*

* GIVEN a user attempts to end a maintenance
* AND at least one Change is still in “Implement”
* THEN the system:
** Shows a warning requiring user acknowledgment

----

h3. *AC5 – No Impact from Overlapping Maintenance*

* GIVEN multiple maintenance windows exist on the same instance
* THEN sub-status behavior is controlled only by Change Requests

----

h3. *AC6 – Scope Control*

* GIVEN Change Requests not linked to the maintenance
* THEN they are NOT considered in validation or sub-status logic

----

h3. *AC7 – System warning* 

* when a MW is move to Start and End there is a warning to say that Instances will be in sub-status, need to remove that, and add a sentence to MWM to ensure that users will change CR to implement.
* The exact sentence that need to be removed is: the creation of cases will be disabled from alert/alarm 
* the exact sentence that need to be is: Please note on changing the status to start maintenance, the publication is going to be sent to the publication customers-related list, the publication will be displayed in the portal and under the instances, and a message will be sent to the Change request owner, please check the CR owner move the status of the change to disable creation of cases

----

h3. *AC8 – CR Substatus removal functionality*  



If there is two CR working in parallel and the first one have been ended, the substatus should stay till all CR is completed

----

h2. *Additional Details / Considerations*

* *Operational benefit:*
** Eliminates false case creation during ongoing maintenance work
** Improves monitoring accuracy and alert suppression
* *Process alignment:*
** Fully aligns with standard Change Management lifecycle (Implement → Review).
* *Edge cases to consider:*
** Very large maintenance scopes (e.g., thousands of CIs) may impact performance
** Users must follow correct Change lifecycle updates to avoid unintended alerts
* *Interim workaround (current state):*
** Manage all related work within a single maintenance window to avoid duplicate behavior issues.

column1: Cloud Request - 'Pending Resubmit'
column36:
For some category
An approval process exists
If the user rejected
Status changed to Resolved/Rejected
The user can update the form
change the status 'Pending Resubmit.'
Press the 'Resubmit' button
The status changed to 'Pending Approval.'
and the user has the ability to Reject/Approve again.

Requirement -Create approval loop – if rejected, enable user to resubmit the form and go to pending approval.

*Workato Recipe Logic:*

# Workato Recipe 56162808 (SF2CB Amendments) — before each Track_User_Fields API call to Cadebill (table: customer_product_instance), a conditional step checks whether the product's start_date is greater than the requested end_date.
# If start_date > end_date (or start_date = end_date), the recipe overrides end_date = start_date + 1 day before sending the payload to Cadebill.
# If start_date <= end_date (product is active or end date is valid), no override is applied and the original end_date is used.
# The Workato job log records the original end_date and the overridden value whenever a substitution occurs, for audit purposes.

*Pre-Condition:*

column36:
h2. Requirements

*Purpose:*

The *NSC Tickets Agent* (Incident or Request) enables BA CS and BA Cadebill teams to resolve NSC tickets faster by retrieving historically similar tickets from ServiceNow and presenting AI‑assisted resolution recommendations.

The agent analyses and classifies the ticket, assigns it to a generic user, automatically updates its status, and based on the ticket description, generates a structured set of recommended insights.

 

*High-Level Behavior:*

* When an Incident or Request is assigned to the BA CS, BA Cadebill, or BA Fin Cadebill teams, the agent automatically classifies the ticket and assigns it to the designated user (Eitan Fireberg).
* The agent updates the ticket status to “Pending Future Activities” and sets a target date two weeks from the creation date.
* The agent changes the ticket status to “Pending Future Activities” with a Target Date of 2 weeks ahead.
* The agent is integrated with all NSC tickets managed by these teams.
* Upon assignment, the agent searches for historically similar NSC tickets and provides references to related cases, along with recommended next steps or resolution actions. These insights are automatically added to the ticket’s Work Notes.

column1: Committed Quantity Automation Business Rule - New Requirement
column36:
*Background*: When we launched the automation we faced a challenge. The underlying rule was that SOFTW and SOFTU (Software MRC & Usage) will be transferred with a quantity of 1. But there were several exceptions – for specific SKUs and specific SKUs per specific partner (RingCentral & Verizon).

There was no +SF+ +identifier+ for the relevant SKUs, so we relied on SKU External Description and asked MCL to create a business rule for all the SKUs which should be entered with quoted quantity.

!image-20251117-053845.png|width=259,height=94,alt="image-20251117-053845.png"!



Maintaining this list would be a nightmare and prone to errors.

Since then, we moved RingCentral automation to rely on Unit of Measure Business Rule.

For each SKU, *Workato* will “look” at the SKU page and for identified Unit of Measure and Partner RingCentral, will transfer the quoted quantity

!image-20251117-053919.png|width=520,height=279,alt="image-20251117-053919.png"!



Now, SF has created a field on the SKU level, like Unit of Measure, defining whether the SKU should be billed by contracted quantity or higher or normally according to usage.

*SKU API :* +*Contracted_QTY__c*+

 

+*The request*+

# Create a new generic Business Rule: For Product Family “Software MRC” or “Software Usage” Workato will look at the SKU “Contracted_QTY__c” and if True will transfer to Cadebill the quoted “Quantity”
# In Parallel, create “Verizon Contracted Quantity” BR.
## If opp Partner Account INCLUDES Verizon AND
## Account “Government Account” is FALSE
## Then for selected SKUs (existing BR SKUs under Verizon) => enter “Quantity” to Cadebill
# Once this is in place, the existing Contracted Quantity BR can be retired   (you can build #2 based on it as well, whatever works)

 

 

After that, whenever CPQ defines a new SKU, it will determine whether it is committed quantity True.

column1: Enhancement to CSM Assignment Logic in Wiser
column36:
*Current Behavior:*

Currently, if a solution-level CSM field is left blank, the system automatically inherits the Customer-level CSM. This behavior prevents users from intentionally leaving the solution-level CSM field empty in cases where no CSM should be assigned to a specific solution.

*Problem Statement:*

There is a business scenarios where a Customer-level CSM does not cover all solutions under the account. In such cases, need the ability to leave the solution-level CSM field blank to indicate that no CSM is assigned. The current logic does not support this and automatically overwrites the blank field with the Customer-level CSM. If the CSM field Manually removed - need to remain blank.

*Proposed Change:*

If the CSM field Manually removed - need to remain blank

column1: Require Status Change When "Restored" Checkbox is Unchecked
column36:
h3. *Require Status Change When "Restored" Checkbox is Unchecked*

Currently, when the "Restored" checkbox is unchecked on critical cases, the case status remains as "Restored," which can lead to inconsistencies in SLA tracking and case handling.

To improve this behavior, we propose the following change:

* *Trigger*: When the "Restored" checkbox is unchecked
* *Validation*: If the case status is still set to "Restored," prompt the user to change the status before allowing the checkbox to be unchecked.
* *Purpose*: This ensures that engineers cannot uncheck the "Restored" checkbox while the case is still in "Restored" status, enforcing a proper status transition (e.g., to "WIP" or another appropriate status).

*Expected Outcome*:
Engineers must update the case status from "Restored" to another valid status before they can uncheck the "Restored" checkbox. This prevents logical inconsistencies and ensures accurate SLA tracking.

manage a template, to enable the owner to edit some input should be auto populated (template added in the end of the file)

column1: Free Months up to $ minimum
column36:
As part of phase 2, and following ELT decision in the last steering committee, I believe we need development from MCL, to support the new free months phrasing, *up to the contracted minimum.*

 

+*The new phrasing:*+

 

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Order: (a) the Subscription Term will commence on the Order Effective Date; and (b) solely during the first XXXXX (X) months of the Subscription Term (the “No Charge Period”), Customer may use the Cloud Services set forth in Section 1/Table 1(X) above, excluding success packages, at no charge, up to the amount of the Minimum Monthly Recurring Charge or Minimum Monthly Commitment specified in Section 1/Table 1(X) (the “No Charge Cloud Services”).  Customer will be responsible for any usage of Cloud Services during the No Charge Period that exceeds the No Charge Cloud Services. 

 

For example, if the Minimum Monthly Recurring Charge or Minimum Monthly Commitment is $10,000, Customer may use up to $10,000 worth of Cloud Services at no charge during each month of the No Charge Period. If Customer's usage of Cloud Services in a given month of the No Charge Period has a value of $12,000, Customer will be responsible for payment of $2,000 for usage in excess of the No Charge Cloud Services.

 

 

Until now Cadebill just calculated whether the customer is below the minimum.

Now, during free months, Cadebill will need to calculate whether the customer is above the minimum in a particular month and add Charge for usage above the minimum.

column1: Motorola CR
column36:
After investigating, we found details about the integration between Motorola ServiceNow and Wiser (Michelle's design document is attached).

This integration allows the following actions:

 

* An API call is triggered from Motorola to Wiser with details for requesting the creation of a case. Wiser then creates the case and sends back the details.
* The next step involves comments. The business reason for the comments is to facilitate communication between NICE and Motorola. However, the issue is that every comment added to the case, whether internal or external, is marked as an external comment.



Another problem is that every comment received in their system creates an "acknowledge" notification in Wiser, which triggers another external comment sent to Motorola.

They have requested the following changes:

* Align the system so that only external comments are sent via API.
* Remove the "acknowledge" notification to prevent the addition of irrelevant comments to their ServiceNow.

 

On the technical side, we have reviewed the situation and can make these changes specifically for Motorola. As shown below, we can modify the call based on IP or name.

More than that after reviewing with Ricky (Rivka Beker) we understand that in the integration itself we are not indicating if the comment is internal or external, it happens in Wiser.

12/Jan/25 8:59 AM;621f1c4f94f7e20069fdd50c;*COMM1635222 Commented: Multiple Instances Multi-factor authentication notification: Review NICE Ltd*

*Multi-factor authentication Notification*
*Review • December 2024*



We will begin enforcing Multi-factor authentication (MFA) for non-SSO logins starting with the Now Platform^®^ Yokohama release planned for March 2025, which will enhance security and provide a more robust defense against potential security threats.



*Here’s what you can expect*



Beginning with the Now Platform^®^ Yokohama release planned for March 2025, Multi-factor authentication will be turned on by default in all instances. This initiative underscores our commitment to enhancing security across the platform. Please find key details below:



# *No Impact on SSO Logins and Integrations*



MFA enforcement will apply *exclusively* to username and password-based UI logins. Single Sign-On (SSO) logins and integrations remain unaffected.



 



# *MFA Enrollment Requirement*



Users performing username and password-based logins (excluding snc_external users) will be required to set up MFA. Upon their first successful local login after the Yokohama upgrade, each user will have a 30-day window to self-enroll in MFA.



 



# *Administrator Flexibility*



Administrators will have the ability to modify the MFA policy to extend the enrollment window or exempt specific users, roles, or groups from the MFA requirement, if necessary.



Please review this [KB1700938|https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB1700938] or the [MFA FAQ|https://support.servicenow.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sysparm_article=KB1709783] for more details.



In addition, beginning with the Now Platform^®^ Australia release planned for March 2026, we will deprecate the glide.authenticate.multifactor property that allows customers to disable Multi-factor authentication.



 



*Here’s what we need you to do*



Start planning, you have two options:



* You can configure MFA before upgrading to Yokohama. Review the Multi-factor authentication (MFA) [+product documentation+|https://www.servicenow.com/docs/bundle/xanadu-platform-security/page/integrate/authentication/concept/mfa-config-landing.html] to learn how to configure MFA for your instances ahead of your migration to ensure the smoothest roll-out possible
* We will keep this Communication record open for 4 weeks to allow for any necessary documentation and planning.

08/Oct/24 10:58 AM;6114ed43e6e6f80071784a76;TBU calculation on the case is the same as in the Task/SR:

•	The TBU calculation is based all ENU SLA of the request while at least one SLA should be marked with 'Has Breached' True (including cancelled SLAs).
•	Following is the TBU calculation in Request table:
o	Sum up the “Business elapsed time” of all ENU SLA of the request (Business duration is the “Business elapsed time” from the Task SLA. It measures working hours’ time since the “Start time“ from the Task SLA).
o	Reduce the SLA Duration of the Breached SLA.

o	The TBU is:
1 - (Business elapsed time-Duration) / Business elapsed time)

•	The TBU represents 1 minus the deviation ratio between the time allocated to the SLA and the time it took.
o	When there is no deviation the TBU will be 1.
o	When there is a big deviation the TBU will be a number closer to zero.
o	When there is a small deviation the TBU will be a number closer to 1.

19/Aug/24 1:37 PM;6114ed43e6e6f80071784a76;Silver reply to why Impact Duration is empty:

I'll explain here the behavior of the case, so you don't need to read previous messages:

When Jeff approved the tasks, this business rule was triggered:
[https://nicetest.service-now.com/sys_script.do?sys_id=d535fa571b848114d8d9ec22b24bcb68|https://nicetest.service-now.com/sys_script.do?sys_id=d535fa571b848114d8d9ec22b24bcb68|smart-link] 
This BR puts the field u_downtime(System Down)=true, which triggers the next BR:

[https://nicetest.service-now.com/sys_script.do?sys_id=1cd633e81bae4510ef55a7d5604bcb5c|https://nicetest.service-now.com/sys_script.do?sys_id=1cd633e81bae4510ef55a7d5604bcb5c|smart-link] 
This BR sets the Restoration(u_dt_end) field, in this particular case to empty because of the conditions of the script.

As the Restoration field changes, the next BR is triggered: [https://nicetest.service-now.com/sys_script.do?sys_id=217618f81b628510ef55a7d5604bcb04|https://nicetest.service-now.com/sys_script.do?sys_id=217618f81b628510ef55a7d5604bcb04|smart-link] 

This BR takes the differences between the start date and the restoration date, and set Impact duration field as the value of the difference, but since restoration was empty, the difference cannot be computed and an empty value in returned. Hence, the impact duration is also set ot empty.

Issue: 
* Our internal monitoring system triggered the following alert " Performance Impact - Users Affected - Default Semaphore Impacted niceprod" 
Most Probable Cause: 
* The instance stats intermittent spike in Default semaphore usage between 11:30 and 14:30 PST, Jan 30

* The cause of the low memory conditions on impacted nodes was due to long running /api/now/graphql transactions triggered by 
[Jashleen.Channey@nice.com|mailto:Jashleen.Channey@nice.com]

Solution Proposed: 
* The transactions are no longer running and the instance response time is back to normal state. 
Next Steps: 
* Please review and let us know if you have any further questions or comments. 

Best regards, 
Meera|

column36:
Cause:

The standard URL length is limited to 2083 characters, and if a request URL surpasses this limit, a 414 Error is triggered. In the case of the export PDF API request, the URL had a length of approximately 151304 characters, which caused the error and consequently resulted in the export failure.
This lengthy URL is generated as a result of the filter values that were entered into the filter modal of the list.



Workaround Solution:
To address the 414 Error problem, I've devised a solution involving the creation of script include, which can provide us with filter values.

For instance:

In the filter modal to obtain the value for the Number filter, use the following code: javascript:new testScript().getNumbers().
The getNumbers method will provide all the case numbers that require filtering.
Implementing this approach will result in shorter URLs, ultimately enabling us to successfully generate exports.

23/Jan/24 2:39 PM;70121:33c9c08c-01ca-4a34-ac93-994a2946b894;Gerhard’s answer regarding the OpsGenie Alert:



I’m reducing the audience a little bit. Reut, your suggestion to move all this into Wiser will not work, at least not for Cloud Operations. You cannot determine the assignment group based on the source of the alert. In other words, I cannot look at Pingdom as the source and then use that as the logic to say all Pingdom alerts will go to this group. We make very granular changes to individual alerts as to who they need to go to. So unless you want to hire an FTE whose only job is to come up with a few hundred assignment rules, I’d steer away from that proposal. Cloudwatch is another example. CloudWatch simply reflects a monitoring tool. It doesn’t dictate who gets the alert. Cloudwatch can identify a problem with an RDS service in which case it may go to the database team for some product or to the AppOps team for others, as different teams have different requirements as to who gets the alerts.

 

What I can suggest is that you may have logic that says if the tag WiserGroup in the alert does NOT exist, we can assign to certain groups based on the logic that other teams may be able to provide you. But if the tag does exist in the alert then the tag will have to be used to decide who to assign an alert/case to. It may be that other teams can break it up that way, but it will not work for us. But I doubt that you will be able to assign it correctly for other teams as well if you simply base it on the source of the alert.

 

Thanks.

column1: Quality process - Internal notification
column36:
Once a quality notification is sent, a message is displayed in the 'Notes and Activity' tab with the following:

Case Quality Results for Case {number} 

 

However, since this is an internal comment the system sends an internal notification which is sent always after an internal comment (this existing notification is sent to the owner and to the internal list).

This notification is detail the internal comment but also adds before the comment +the user that wrote the comment+ and the comment date.

 

We have 2 options here:

# Disable this internal comment in case the internal comment is "Case Quality Results for Case {number}".
# Create a new internal notification that will be the same as the existing one but without specifying the user that wrote the comment.

column1: glide.smtp.send_partial
column36:
Create this new glide record for partial email send if there’s wrong email addresses in the recipients list



{{glide.smtp.send_partial}}

Splits outgoing email between valid and invalid recipients. The email is sent only to the valid recipients. A new email containing the invalid recipients is created in the *send-ready* state and attempts to send again.

* Type: true | false
* Default value: false



If one of the recipients is not valid then the email record would be updated by the system with the state as "Ready" and Type as "send-retry-delayed".This is performed by the system in an attempt to reprocess the email. 

Adding the following property 'glide.smtp.send_partial' with the value 'TRUE' should help to resolve the issue. 

For more details on resolution refer KB below- 
[KB1261730 : Email records are stuck in "Ready" state with Type as "send-retry-delayed"|https://hi.service-now.com/kb?id=kb_article_view&sys_kb_id=ef5289991b7ce550546e35df034bcbda]

column1: Create Wiser report for variables and question choice
column36:
Please create a report of all variables & question choices so I'll be able to compare data to fivetran.

The fields I'm using are: (it’s the query I'm using which has all joins and fields so you can build a similar Wiser report)

 

For variable:

*select* im.request_item_value *as* request_code,i_n.CAT_ITEM_VALUE , Q.*name* *as* db_field_name, META.sys_name *AS* app_field_name,  i.value,i.ITEM_OPTION_NEW_VALUE

*from* FIVETRAN_DATABASE.WISER_PROD.SC_ITEM_OPTION_MTOM *as* im

*join* FIVETRAN_DATABASE.WISER_PROD.SC_ITEM_OPTION *as* i *on* im.SC_ITEM_OPTION_VALUE = i.sys_id

*join* FIVETRAN_DATABASE.WISER_PROD.ITEM_OPTION_NEW i_n *on* i.item_option_new_value = i_n.sys_id 

*JOIN* FIVETRAN_DATABASE.WISER_PROD.QUESTION *as* Q *ON* i.ITEM_OPTION_NEW_VALUE =Q.SYS_ID

*JOIN* FIVETRAN_DATABASE.WISER_PROD.SYS_METADATA *AS* meta *ON* i.ITEM_OPTION_NEW_VALUE = META.sys_id

 

For question choice:

*select* n.cat_item_value,*t*.*name* *as* db_field_name,  y.value,y."TEXT"

*from* FIVETRAN_DATABASE.WISER_PROD.ITEM_OPTION_NEW n

*join* FIVETRAN_DATABASE.WISER_PROD.QUESTION *t* *on* n.sys_id = *t*.sys_id

*join* FIVETRAN_DATABASE.WISER_PROD.QUESTION_CHOICE y *on* *t*.sys_id = y.question_value

column36:
Template name is: *Low Volume – Workflow Health Check*

Relevant for NIA/QC solutions.

Cases where Functionality = Low Volume

Cloud/hosted only. The template is to populate in the internal comments section (not external comments). 

Once saved, the comment should be populated in the Internal Comments and an email sent to the following internal ppl: Jeffrey Strnad, Ofir Shemesh, Erik Sebold, Ajay Kumar, TAM (if exist at the Wiser), and all internal members mentioned in the “Internal List” of the case.  Subject line: Impact Case____, Customer, Low Volume Workflow Health Check” (case and customer populated automatically)

New Template text is below, where [   ] indicates automatically populated field:



Dear Nexidia Management team,

A Low Volume [Impact] case [Case_____] has been created on [date time].



_“Workflow Health Check Validated - Case move to Monitor._ 

Customer Name: (auto pop)

Instance Name: (auto pop)

Case Impact: (auto pop)

Description: (auto pop)

_1. Extractor\Ingest:_

* _Based on 'Interactions Sent To Ingested' – What is last submitted date? How many hours since last activity? What is the threshold?_ 
* _Based on ‘Interactions Ingested’ – What is last ingested date? How many hours since last activity? What is the threshold?_  

_2. ETL – Based on ‘NIA Jobs’ – Core Update ETL – ‘Last Success Date’ - When was the last successful ETL run? Higher than 4 hours?_

_3. ASR:_

* _Based on Discovery\Update\ETL – ‘Last Success Date’ - When was the last successful ASR run? Higher than 4 hours?_
* _Based on Interaction ASR – ‘Hours Since Last Activity’ - When was the last successful ASR run per source? Higher than 4 hours?_

_4. DEU – Based on DEU report – What is Hours Since Last Activity? Does it miss the threshold (only on sources that have Threshold set)?_

 _Next update ETA: In X hours.”_

column1: Actimize watch DataOps - email to case
column36:
We spoke about this several times in the past,

 

We have in Actimize Watch a team of "DataOps" these guys analyze the Actimize Watch product logs and nowadays they open a ticket in Jira by sending an email to Jira (BTW, Actimize Watch is a cloud product)

 

This is causing an operational challenge as the content should be addressed to the PS TAMs that work in Wiser.

The logs are per customer tenant – meaning Instance (kind of monitoring but that analysis is done manually for now)

 

In different scenarios, once the PS team completed the internal analysis and actions, they are required to expose the issue to the customer (externalize a case) – today it’s mainly done via emails…

 

I explored the option of opening a manual internal case manually.

 

It's causing other changes, such as,

# Each customer must have a team line project.
# We cannot leverage the "externalize case" functionality.
# The process of opening a case requires more effort than just sending an email…

 

I'm requesting to expand the existing "email to case" functionality that was developed for DataIQ to customize a solution for "Actimize Watch"

 

By adding an additional platform defined as "Actimize Watch" and defining for the DataOps a unique email they should send the email from and defining the email subject mask to include the instance number – we can relatively easily provide a solution that is very similar to the way they work with Jira today.

 *1.* helpful *2.* not helpful *3.* X to close the message.

* Option to show the pop-up in different terms for external or internal users (every KA viewed for internal and with exceptions for external)
* Option to pop-up the message every 10th (or X times) KA

* The article is published

column1: Create new SR that will give the customers the ability to track bugs
column36:
Bugs are prioritize based on Bugs in Jira.  It should not be part of ER process.

When the PO gets a bug as a ER (product task) he will reject it as "Not valid ER" and ask to open a bug.

Ideally we wanted that CS will be able to identify that something is a bug and not an enhancement request, and do not send bugs to PO.   Ideally we also discussed that if it happens, then the PO will send it back to CS, ask to cancel the product task and open a bug.

A bug should not sit in the ERs queue. Hence this CR is to create new SR that will give the customers the ability to track bugs

*** 3 month - last full 3 months

column1: Mail needed from Wiser on a regular basis for solution provided yet case being in 'Open' state
column36:
Mail needed from Wiser on a regular basis for solution provided yet Case being in 'Open' state.

The criteria for this list being:

* All Related CS tasks are closed 
* No other Open objects are associated with the case i.e. , enhancement, tasks etc.
* The case is 3 months or older

This should be applied to all cases type, irrelevant to where it was opened from or by who.



* Email notification should be sent to the user (case owner) once the ticket has passed his 3 months life duration, 
* every week another email will be sent with same subject and email body, email +should continue until the case is+ +*closed*++.+
** Text of the email + subject (to case owner)
*** Case <Case number> is open for over 90 days and should be closed ASAP
**** §  Hi <User First name>,
Please keep in mind that <case number> is open for over 90 days and should be handled and closed ASAP.
The email is being sent when there are no pending tasks, enhancements, etc. to the case.
Please have it closed as soon as possible.
In case the email will not be closed in a week, you and the previous case owner will get notified again until closure.

Thanks.

* -Another email notification should be sent to the- *-previous-* -case owner (in case there is one) and will be sent 1 week after the first email that was sent to the case owner and should be sent repetitively every two weeks.-
** -Text of the email + subject (To previous case owner)-
*** -Case <Case number> is opened for over 90 days and should be closed-
**** -Hi <User First name>,-
-Please keep in mind that <case number> that you were the previous owner of - is open for over 90 days and should be closed ASAP.-
-This email is sent when there are no pending tasks, enhancements, etc. to the case.-
-You are getting this email as you are the previous case owner, and the current owner didn’t act on it in the past week after being mailed regarding the above.-
-Please make sure to have it closed as soon as possible.-

-Thanks.-

customer

impact

within Bus hours and out of Bus hours 

time outside our control (ie pending customer or third party) is not counted against in the SLAs

manage penalty per tier  

enable functionality of - “mutually agreed upon time to fix”. To cover scenarios where we agree with the customer a fix needs to happen in maintenance window or gets deferred for any reason --> open issue if stops SLA or enable entering new target

|S3 Response Time|Next business day|No penalty|
|S4 Response Time|Next business day|No penalty|

column1: Create Calendar Appointments in Wiser
column36:
Please find below requirements and high-level customer experience flow, let me know when you want to discuss.

 __ 
 * 'Set A Meeting' button will initially appear when a case: 'Assigned to Engineer' and Status is 'WIP' and only to Critical and High case impact (this will change latter on and include also 'Medium' and 'Low' once we will work with it for a while)
 * After clicking the button from Portal / Tech View pop up with the engineer calendar will appear (owner of the case)

 * TZ – to set the Engineer calendar according to the Customer TZ​
 * Meeting slot will be 30 min.
 * Option to extend to another 30 min / to close the calendar 30 min before and after a meeting  ​​


 * Calendar will open for 48 hours availability slots
 * If there are no slots available to jump a day forward, and share notification to the engineer about a far a way meeting schedule so he can try to promote​

 
 * Set a Meeting option after re-assignment of a case will open the current case owner calendar​​
 * Option to add to the meeting CSM / TAM / others Nice employees / other external contacts related to the customer ​ ​
 * Set a Meeting option will be unavailable when the case status is "new", "resolved", "closed"​, planned meeting​
 * Holidays / Weekends – the functionality will not be available during the weekend and holidays and the calendars will be unavailable for meeting during Holidays and Weekends  

 
 * Integration with Teams should support the option that if engineer calendar is available but he is in a call than it will show as unavailable to set a meeting
 * Another option is to close the calendar half an hour after assigned to a case ('go over the case' time before customer can set a meeting)

 
 * Meeting subject: NICE Support Meeting *Case#*,*Customer#*, *Case Owner*​
 * Meeting Invite: will contain link to Wiser Portal and Case, Link to reschedule or cancel the meeting 
 * Meeting Invite will send to Engineer and Customer Emails so they can approve, reject or reschedule the meeting – approving the meeting will set it in their calendar
 * Add a Flag that customer has approved the meeting
 * Meeting Invite will sent as BCC to the Engineer manager and the assigned TAM as default.
 * Meeting Invite will sent as "Nice Customer Support" from any domain

 
 * Meeting Notes section will appear as part of the case after the call ended (Template in the Case handling form with main decisions and next steps)​ and will be sent to customer from Wiser

 
 * If a case already have a meeting set, the date and time will appear next to the 'Set A Meeting' button
 * If a case already have a meeting set, another meeting can’t be set​ to the same day from the customer side 
 * If a case already have a meeting set, no limitation from the engineer side  
 * If a case already have a meeting set, the meeting slot can be rescheduled ​
 * The meeting slot can be rescheduled until the start time of the meeting​
 * If a case already have a meeting set, the meeting slot can be cancelled​
 * The meeting slot can be cancelled until the start time of the meeting​

 
 * If a case already have a meeting set and the engineer assigned the case to a higher tier, a reschedule notification will be send to the customer with the current case owner calendar ​

 
 * Notification – in creation, change or cancel, meeting notes after the call ended, pre-meeting (1/2 h) ​

 
 * Case can't be resolved with a future scheduled meeting, Support needs to get the customer consent to cancel the meeting before Case resolved

just to align everyone, this refers to the tables that appear in tabs at the bottom of forms (like the case form). Those are currently loaded together with the form fields. 2. On demand option - the system will not load the lists at all, but there will be a button at the bottom of the form where the user can click on and this will load the lists.

column1: Number of records to display in lists
column36:
we currently allow users to display up to 100 records in one page when looking at lists.

This substantially affects the loading times. Not just of lists, also of other entities that include lists (like homepages). One of their most interesting insights was that not only this affects the person himself, but consumes system resources that basically affect the whole instance behavior. Imagine just 100 of the ~700 users with this setting loading a list at the same time... probably happens.
 Their recommendation is to default all users to 20 records per list. And also remove the option of 100 at all. Leave 50 as the highest one possible to choose by users.

column1: MACD SR adjustments to serve AMS requirements
column36:
Name for Service Request – “*Managed Services – Service Request*”

the SR will be opened when customer will need AMS assistance on the following items - 

Business queries 
 Deployments
 Data extract from System
 On-Prem Environment provisioning 
 Reports Management/ DART
 Data Validation
 Tuning Support
 Display Changes/Dashboards/Work Items Changes
 Workflow Changes/Configurations 
 On-Prem Permissions
 General Request

 

justifications:
 # Service requests are different from Issues for which incident tickets are raised at WISER, These types of requests can be of some specific information requested or enhancement/service required by client. It is very difficult to manage such service requests as WISER incident tickets, also there are no single Service request forms available which can be used for this purpose. At Actimize- AMS level we need a service request form which can be used.

 

-By various clients as single point to raise the various types service requests. We can give option to client to raise specific Service requests based on the drop down field "Service Request Type". This way client's confusion can be eliminated and they can raise all AMS related service request at single form to AMS instead of raising the AMS SRs to incorrect teams

 

-This will also ensure the AMS related service request will fall into AMS bucket and not on undesired bucket which could result delay in delivering the SRs to client.

 

-As AMS service requests are different from WISER Incident tickets, and we have separate contracts for SRs especially for Essentials and hosted clients, this separate SR form for AMS will also ease the management, categorization and report creation of Service Requests which needs to be shared with client and higher management periodically.

column1: New API to retrieve contact information

Currently, this is a manual export of contacts from Wiser which means I keep forgetting to do it etc.

 # Active contacts (only)

 # Contact Email
 # Customer Name [the name of the organization, not the contact]

Provide a JSON format dump (similar to the Wiser to Zoomin existing API)

I believe my original request was to be able to import using a SKU instead of requiring the CPID.  For the Billing team, looking up the CPID is manual and time consuming especially if there are several or many records to import.  We plan to use this rebill import when LiveVox is integrated into Cadebill and there will likely be hundreds of LiveVox imports monthly beginning in January.

We can test this new import function and roll that into Production as Step 1.  My request is that we figure out Step 2 which would be uploading Quantity by Account, SKU (parts) and Chargedate.  Thoughts?
